I have been working this land for 40 years. I know what grows here and what doesn't. My body is older now, some of my children earn wages in the city, so I must be practical about what I can manage alone or with my wife.

My 11.4 mu I will split the usual way — about 8 mu stays in wheat and maize rotation, the rest I keep in cotton. Cotton prices have been decent and I know how to grow it, even if it wears me out in August.

**Wheat (winter, 8 mu):** I plant every October after the maize comes off. I'll use the Jimai improved variety — it performs reliably here and the seed station sells it. I apply base fertilizer before sowing: diammonium phosphate plus urea. I top-dress at jointing. I irrigate four times: at sowing, at jointing, at heading, and at grain filling — that is what we do here, the soil dries out badly in spring. Two sprays for aphids and powdery mildew, that is usually enough. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

**Maize (summer, 8 mu):** Goes in right after wheat harvest in June. No time to plough — I use the rotary cutter and direct seed. Zhengdan 958 hybrid, I have planted it for years. Heavy on nitrogen — maize here needs it. Two or three irrigations. Usually just two pesticide sprays unless there is armyworm pressure.

**Cotton (spring–autumn, 3.4 mu):** I start preparing in April. Hybrid Bt cotton variety — fewer sprays needed than the old types, though I still spray seven or eight times over the season because pests here are bad in July. Cotton needs careful irrigation and I have the well, so I manage. It is the most labor-intensive work I do all year, but the income is important.

I will not change much from last year. My yields are steady. At my age I am not experimenting.
